what_is_at_risk: The equity of every other borrower (holder of debt shares), because the top-up minted at seize raises the total debt balance and so raises every other position's debt in the debt token (DETH).
who_loses: Other borrowers with open debt. Their debt grows by their share of the top-up. If their position goes underwater, the excess becomes new bad debt, which in the end dilutes holders of the debt token (DETH) such as liquidity providers.
who_gains: The attacker who owns the position and seizes it through a helper contract.
scenario: A victim borrower holds 10 TOKEN as collateral and owes 9 DETH. The attacker deposits 0.5 TOKEN, borrows 1 DETH, seizes its own position through a helper inside the same unlock, takes the 1 DETH top-up, repays all its debt and withdraws its 0.5 TOKEN, all in one transaction.
unit: DETH (debt token, 1 DETH = 1e18 wei). TOKEN and DETH are both priced at 1 by the oracle mock.
worst_case_pct_of_user_funds: 100% of other borrowers' equity. In one transaction their debt can grow by up to about 200% (measured 199.8%).
worst_case_basis: The attacker repays inside the same unlock, so its position never needs to be healthy after the seize. Its profit is the top-up (twice the deficit) times the other borrowers' share of total debt, and this tends to twice their debt as the borrow grows. The sweep measured 17.98 DETH profit (victim debt 9 -> 26.98 DETH against 10 TOKEN collateral) with 0.5 TOKEN collateral and a 9,000 DETH borrow, which is under the test's 10,000 DETH debt limit.
scales_with: Total debt of the other borrowers (the profit tends to twice that) and the size of the attacker's borrow. The global debt limit caps the borrow. The attacker only needs a tiny amount of collateral, no flash loan and no price move.
fix_check: The attack reverts with CannotSeizeRegisteredPosition() (selector 0x4c2e8700) at every borrow size. Attacker profit is 0 and victim loss is 0.
note: Denominator = the victim's deposited collateral (10 TOKEN = 10 DETH). The same 0.9 DETH loss is 10% of the victim's debt and 90% of the victim's equity (1 DETH -> 0.1 DETH), and it leaves the victim's position unhealthy, so a liquidator can now seize it. who_loses: Honest liquidity providers whose rewards are still unclaimed (the last LPs to claim also cannot withdraw their liquidity).

what_is_at_risk: No user funds. TimedAdminFacet in the itos-finance Commons library holds no ether or tokens, and its owner role only grants and removes admin rights. What breaks is the ability to hand the owner role to a new address.
who_loses: No one loses funds. The protocol team cannot move the owner role to a new address.
scenario: The owner calls transferOwnership(0xBEEF) and waits past the delay. The pending owner's acceptOwnership reverts, the old owner keeps control and can still grant admin rights, and a second transferOwnership reverts ExistingPrecommitFound because the first request can never be used or cancelled. No ether moved: facet, old owner and new owner balances were unchanged.
worst_case_basis: No function in TimedAdminFacet, BaseAdminFacet or AdminLib moves value. The bug only stops the owner role from changing hands, and the current owner keeps every power it had.
fix_check: The pending owner accepts and the owner becomes 0xBEEF. The new owner can start another transfer and grant rights. 0 wei moved, the same as on the vulnerable code.
note: The test does not measure a loss. It records who controls the contract after the failed handover and checks that no ether moved. what_is_at_risk: Every asset held by a Sequence v3 wallet that sits behind a checkpointer: native ETH and any tokens the wallet owns.
who_loses: The wallet owner (the users of the current, updated wallet configuration).
who_gains: A signer who was removed from the wallet configuration but still appears in the stale configuration stored on chain.
scenario: A Stage1 wallet deployed for config1 (Alice, threshold 1, checkpoint 1) holds 100 test ETH and 1,000,000 MOCK tokens; the checkpointer reports config2 (Bob only, checkpoint 2), so Alice is evicted. Alice's normal signature is rejected (UnusedSnapshot), but the same payload wrapped in a chained signature with the checkpointer bit unset is executed and sends all ETH and all MOCK to Alice.
unit: ETH (test ether set with vm.deal; the MOCK token result is in notes)
worst_case_basis: The bypass yields a signature the wallet accepts as fully valid, and a valid signature authorises any batch of calls, including transfers of every asset and a config update that locks out the real owners. So the evicted signer can take everything the wallet holds.
scales_with: The wallet's total balance across all assets. It also needs the evicted signer (or signers) to reach the threshold of the stale configuration still stored on chain.
fix_check: Attack rejected: execute reverted (empty revert data) and the wallet kept 100 ETH and 1,000,000 MOCK, so loss is 0. The control (direct signature) is still rejected with UnusedSnapshot (0xccbb534f). The exact revert reason under the fix was not decoded.

what_is_at_risk: The winnings owed to the winner of an accepted bet, which is the losing side's stake, paid in the bet's ERC20 token (USDC in the deployed product).
who_loses: The party who would have won the bet. They get only their own stake back and lose the winnings.
who_gains: The losing party. The taker can call cancel directly; the maker cannot, but any other address the maker controls can. The losing party gets back a stake they should have forfeited.
scenario: Maker and taker each stake 1,000 tokens of a local USDC-like mock (6 decimals), the taker accepts, and time moves to one second before the end time; the judge would rule for the maker. The losing taker calls cancel: both get 1,000 back, so the maker receives 1,000 instead of the 2,000 that resolve pays (baseline measured at 2,000).
unit: mock USDC-like token, whole tokens (6 decimals; not real money)
worst_case_pct_of_user_funds: 100% of the winner's winnings on every active bet; as a share of the pot it is takerStake / (makerStake + takerStake), so it approaches 100% when the winner's own stake is small (measured 90.9% at stakes of 100 and 1,000).
worst_case_basis: Cancel refunds each stake, so the winner always loses the whole of the other side's stake and never loses their own principal. The share of the pot lost therefore depends only on the stake ratio, and either losing side can do it on any active bet before the judge resolves.
scales_with: The losing side's stake in each bet, and the number of active bets whose likely outcome becomes visible before the judge resolves them.
fix_check: Every non-judge cancel (taker and third party) reverts with Unauthorized() (0x82b42900). The judge then resolves and the maker receives the full pot (2,000, or 1,100 in the uneven case), so the loss is 0 in all three attack cases.
